# Authorisation Risk: {Feature Name}

> See [{product-spec}]({product-spec}) for product context.
> Spec type: authorisation-risk
<!-- Generated by `speed define authorisation-risk <feature>` and reviewed by
     `speed audit`. The `> See` link above is how the auditor finds the
     Product spec, so keep it pointing at specs/product/<feature>.md.

     Every claim in this spec should trace to one of the inputs listed under
     "Source Traceability": the Product, Design, Architecture, Threat Model and
     Compliance specs, or a file in the codebase. Cite code as path:line. -->

## Summary
<!-- Two to four sentences: what the feature exposes, who can reach it, and the
     single highest-rated risk. A reader who stops here should know whether
     this feature changes the project's authorisation posture. -->

## Protected Resources
<!-- Every resource the feature reads, creates, changes or deletes that needs
     an access decision. One row per resource.

     | Resource | Sensitivity | Owner | Introduced or changed by |
     |----------|-------------|-------|--------------------------|
     | Invoice  | Confidential (PII, financial) | Account | S2, S4 |

     Sensitivity uses the classification from the Compliance spec when one
     exists. "Introduced or changed by" cites Product story IDs. -->

## Actors and Roles
<!-- Every principal that can act on a protected resource: end-user roles,
     service accounts, background jobs, admins, anonymous callers.
     Say where each role is defined (Architecture spec or code path). -->

## Permission Matrix
<!-- Role × resource × action. Use allow / deny / conditional, and spell out
     the condition ("own records only", "same tenant", "while status=draft").

     | Role | Resource | Action | Decision | Condition | Story |
     |------|----------|--------|----------|-----------|-------|

     Every Product story that touches a protected resource must appear in at
     least one row. -->

## Enforcement Points
<!-- Where each decision in the Permission Matrix is enforced. Distinguish
     existing enforcement (cite path:line) from enforcement this feature must
     add (cite the Architecture or Tech spec section that will own it).

     | Decision | Layer | Location | Status |
     |----------|-------|----------|--------|
     | Account owner can read Invoice | API middleware | src/api/auth.ts:42 | Existing |
     | Same-tenant check on export    | Service         | (new) per RFC §API Surface | Required | -->

## Threats and Abuse Cases
<!-- Authorisation-relevant threats: privilege escalation, IDOR, confused
     deputy, tenant crossover, missing function-level checks, token misuse.
     Reference Threat Model IDs where they exist; add new ones where the
     feature introduces exposure the Threat Model does not cover. -->

## Compliance Obligations
<!-- Controls from the Compliance spec that apply to this feature, and how the
     Permission Matrix and Enforcement Points satisfy each one.

     | Control | Requirement | Satisfied by | Gap |
     |---------|-------------|--------------|-----|
     | SOC2 CC6.1 | Logical access restricted by role | Enforcement rows 1-3 | None | -->

## Risk Register
<!-- One row per risk. Rating = likelihood × impact (Low / Medium / High /
     Critical). Every High or Critical risk needs a mitigation and a test.

     | ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Rating | Mitigation | Verified by |
     |----|------|------------|--------|--------|------------|-------------|
     | AR1 | Export endpoint skips tenant check | Medium | High | High | Add tenant guard in service layer | AR-T3 | -->

## Test Coverage
<!-- Map each enforcement point and each High/Critical risk to tests.
     Existing tests cite path:line. Missing tests get an ID (AR-T1, AR-T2...)
     and a Given/When/Then description so the Architect can turn them into
     tasks.

     | Test | Covers | Status | Location or description |
     |------|--------|--------|-------------------------|
     | AR-T1 | AR1 | Missing | Given a user in tenant A, when they export tenant B's invoices, then 403 | -->

## Open Questions
<!-- Decisions the inputs did not settle. Name who needs to answer each one
     (product, security, compliance). Write "None" if every decision is
     grounded in an input. -->
